newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re shares leap on takeover news.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re shares leap on takeover news.

text.p: Shares in German reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG soared on Friday morning on news of its plans for a merger which will create the second largest insurance company in Germany.

Munich Re announced overnight it would acquire Victoria Holding AG by merging it with its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit. The company, the world leader in reinsurance, would own between 55 to 60 percent of the merged group, to be called ERGO.
Its shares were up four percent, or 202 marks, at 5,225 marks in pre-bourse electronic trade while the IBIS DAX index was in mild retreat, down 0.14 percent.
"This is a really great solution," said Commerzbank AG insurance analyst Patrizia Novak or the merger deal.
"It is somewhat surprising as everyone had expected Victoria to be taken over from abroad," Novak added.
"But that said, I still see Munich Re's shares as very expensive."
Novak and other analysts said the merged group would be a strong competitor for market leader Allianz AG, with even stronger positions than Allianz in certain key segments, such as health insurance.
Victoria is a non-life insurance specialist and Hamburg-Mannheimer focuses more on life insurance, making them very complementary partners, analysts said.
However it was difficult to judge what level of synergy effects the merger would bring and when these would come into effect after the initial cost-intensive period of integration.
"On a very rough estimate, I could see synergies of around 400 million marks, maybe by the year 1999 or 2000," said WestLB's head of insurance research Georg Kanders.
Victoria shares were unchanged at 1,820 marks in IBIS trade. "I think Victoria is well valued at this level," Kanders said.
